title: Scalar integration by parts under integrability and supportwise differentiability
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] with their usual Euclidean structures. Let $m\geq1$, let $f,g:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C$ be functions, and let $w\in\mathbf R^m$. Put $S_h=\overline{\{x:h(x)\ne0\}}$ for any such function $h$. Write $D h(x)$ for its real Fréchet derivative (the real-linear map giving its first-order approximation), with value the zero linear map when that derivative does not exist. Assume $f$ is real differentiable at every point of $S_g$ and $g$ is real differentiable at every point of $S_f$. Assume the three complex functions $x\mapsto (D f(x)w)g(x)$, $x\mapsto f(x)(D g(x)w)$ and $x\mapsto f(x)g(x)$ are Lebesgue integrable. Then $$\int_{\mathbf R^m} f(x)(D g(x)w)\,dx=-\int_{\mathbf R^m}(D f(x)w)g(x)\,dx.$$ No differentiability away from the indicated closed supports is assumed.
